close_reason: Landed in 8d12c8e. Every bench b.iter(|| { ... }) invocation in the six remaining bench functions now ends with a semicolon — three already-removed pipeline_* sites no longer exist, the three parse_* and three convert_* now read 'b.iter(|| { ... });'. Statement-vs-expression intent is explicit; clippy pedantic semicolon_if_nothing_returned is satisfied.
description:
What the code does: every `bench_*` function in `crate-jmap-mime/benches/mime_pipeline.rs` ends with a bare `c.bench_function("name", |b| { b.iter(|| { ... }) })` (no trailing semicolon on the `b.iter(...)` call, and no trailing semicolon on the `c.bench_function(...)` call). Both the closure and the outer fn return `()`. Clippy pedantic `semicolon_if_nothing_returned` flags 9 of the closures at lines 261, 272, 283, 296, 309, 322, 338, 351, 364.

What idiomatic Rust would do: terminate the `b.iter(|| { ... });` call with a semicolon to make it explicit that the bench closure returns `()` as a statement, not as the closure's tail expression. The current shape compiles only because `b.iter` returns `()` and the bench function's tail expression is also `()`; a Rust practitioner reading it has to verify the type chain to confirm there is no accidental `Result` dropped on the floor.

Why it matters: this is a small but real signal. In a function that explicitly returns `()`, the trailing-expression form is acceptable for one-line bodies (`fn foo() { do_thing() }`) but reads as careless when the body is a multi-line `b.iter(|| { ... })` with side-effecting work inside. The clippy lint exists because (a) a future change that makes the inner work fallible would silently shadow a returned `Result` and the test would still 'pass' from clippy's perspective, (b) it signals statement-vs-expression intent at every closure-returning-unit call site, and (c) consistency with the bench fns' `fn bench_parse_small(c: &mut Criterion) { ... }` shape (no `-> ()` return type) is preserved by terminating with `;`.

Concrete fix: add `;` after the closing `)` of each `b.iter(...)` invocation. Nine sites in one file. Mechanical.
title: Bench fns close `b.iter(...)` as tail expression — should be `b.iter(...);`
